title: ready-04: per-project settings (.heca/config.toml)
summary: A settings file in the project root, merged over the user's config key by key.
description:
Decision 12 in `~/projects/heca-pro/docs/decisions.md`. heca-pro stores the planner opt-in, the merge setting and notification overrides here; any heca user can use it for anything config.toml holds.

## Current state
- One config file: `heca-config/src/loader.rs:222` reads `config_dir()/config.toml` (`load` at :180). Reload: `heca/src/main.rs:157`.

## Goal
- `.heca/config.toml` in the project root (the folder heca was started in, or the nearest parent that has `.heca/`), merged over the user config **key by key** — any key it sets wins, tables merge, nothing else is replaced.
- Reload picks up changes to either file.
- `heca --show-config` (or the existing config introspection) says which value came from which file.
- Unknown keys reported the same way as in config.toml.

## Independence
Not blocked by any other feature. The language files (P045/T519, F006) will need the same key-by-key merge: whichever lands first writes it as one shared function and the other reuses it — never two merges. Check before starting whether T519 already did.

## Preserve
- No project file → behaviour identical to today.

## Done when
- A project file that sets one theme colour and one key binding changes only those two, in that project only, and survives a reload.

tasks.title: An untrusted project file is announced on every start and reload, never remembered as seen
tasks.description:
BUG found by Antonio 2026-10-01 in the T523 trust notice (merged): the "once" rule keeps announced.json keyed by folder + file hash, remembered FOREVER (heca/src/project_trust.rs notify_if_untrusted, via heca/src/announced.rs first_time). Antonio changed his project file back to content he had been told about earlier and that is still untrusted; heca now ignores the file silently with no notice. announced.json already held that hash while project-trust.json trusts a different one.

Rule: an untrusted file being ignored must always be visible. While a project file is untrusted, notify on every start and every reload. "Once" only means the same notice is not repeated while it is still up in the running session (the notification store's dedup_key already does that for a live notice). Nothing about it is persisted in announced.json.

Fix (heca/src/project_trust.rs): remove the announced::first_time gate from notify_if_untrusted; split the decision into a pure notice_for(&ProjectFile) -> Option<Notification> (None when trusted) so it is testable without the notification runtime; notify_if_untrusted reads the project and sends it. Keep .dedup_key(folder+hash) and .sticky(). Update the module doc ("once per folder and file content (announced)"). announced.rs stays (other callers: expose pane_show_cwd, pane_items/listing).

Tests: the same untrusted content yields a notice every time it is asked (as after a restart), a trusted file yields none; break-checked by putting the first_time gate back and seeing it red.

Branch fix/t523-trust-notice-every-start from origin/main. Antonio checks by eye: edit the project file to content seen before, restart heca: the notice shows.

---

Verification: cargo test -p heca 769 passed; clippy clean; new test (an untrusted file read from disk gives a notice on every ask, a trusted one gives none) break-checked red with the first_time gate put back. tasks.title: Settings defaults come from the embedded config on every loading path
tasks.description:
Approved by Antonio on 2026-10-09: fix in a separate open heca branch, record the work, and open a PR. Discovered during heca-pro T019; that task remains in progress and this is separate open heca work.

Current: config.default.toml:57 defines the window dimensions. heca-config/src/settings/defaults.rs:25 repeats them in Rust, along with other setting values. settings/mod.rs:223 constructs SettingsConfig::default by hand; field-level serde defaults also use the Rust helpers. settings/notifications.rs:5 duplicates nested defaults. Normal loading in loader/mod.rs:32 already starts with embedded TOML and deep_merge (:77). Main has already split the old 697-line settings.rs into a folder; reuse that split.

Goal: config.default.toml owns all SettingsConfig and NotificationSystemConfig defaults. Default constructors, partial direct deserialization, normal loading and project layering agree. Keep public settings types, aliases and explicit overrides compatible.

Pre-flight: reuse loader::CONFIG_DEFAULT and its existing embedded-default parsing pattern (parse_default_keys), and reuse loader::deep_merge for layering. No UI widget, action, or new loading door is needed. Siblings T523 and T533 own project layering and trust notices, respectively; neither owns the duplicated settings defaults.

Implementation: parse the embedded settings table once; use one typed field lookup for serde defaults, without recursively constructing SettingsConfig. Read complete Default constructors from that same table. Remove literal defaults from settings helpers, including nested notifications and enum-valued settings. Add any missing non-optional settings to the default file. Optional overrides stay optional and use any value supplied by the embedded file.

Verify: default constructors and empty/partial deserialization match the file; removing each field preserves its file default; nested defaults and aliases still work; explicit overrides, including zero and false, survive; wrong types remain errors. Run heca-config tests, review against the Rust skill, and run the required clippy checks. Record verification and the PR link. Do not edit the existing shared checkout or heca-pro code.

tasks.title: Declare settings once and generate file defaults
tasks.description:
Approved by Antonio on 2026-10-09: a separate branch, task and PR for removing the repeated setting declarations introduced by T540 / merged PR #285 (71b4b164).

Current: heca-config/src/settings/mod.rs:22 declares SettingsConfig fields and serde callbacks. settings/defaults.rs:39 and :47 register the same field names and types again in required_defaults!/optional_defaults!; settings/notifications.rs:5 repeats nested callback functions. config.default.toml owns the values after T540. This task removes the repeated declarations while preserving that file as the source of defaults.

Pre-flight: reuse defaults::value and its OnceLock raw TOML cache, loader::CONFIG_DEFAULT, and serde's existing container default support. T540 owns moving default values into TOML and is done; T523/T533 own project loading/trust. No existing task owns generating this field wiring. Antonio explicitly approved this follow-up. No UI or widget work is involved.

Implementation: add a private settings declaration macro in settings/schema.rs. Declare each field once with its public type, docs and aliases. Generate the public struct with serde container defaults and a Default implementation that resolves each declared field through one typed lookup using its name and optional nested table path. Remove field registration lists and nested callback boilerplate. Both SettingsConfig and NotificationSystemConfig use the same macro. An absent optional TOML setting remains None through serde's type handling; missing required defaults are embedded-file defects, not user input errors. Do not add dependencies or change callers, public field types, serialized names, config values or deep_merge.

Verify: run existing heca-config tests; cover aliases, nested defaults, explicit zero/false, JSON null and invalid values; demonstrate a new setting needs only its declaration and, if required, a default TOML entry. Check malformed embedded defaults fail clearly. Review against the Rust skill, run required full workspace Clippy, run --show-config, and record the new PR link. Preserve other agents' branches and dirty files. Keep heca-pro T019 in progress.

Branch: refactor/settings-schema in /Users/antonio/projects/heca-settings-schema, based on freshly fetched develop plus merged main so it includes PR #285. PR target: main. Canonical planner: /Users/antonio/projects/heca.
